# Bounded XML tokenizer

`svg_xml_tokenize` reads a borrowed `base_bytes` view and writes caller-owned
`svg_xml_token` entries. It never allocates, reads files, resolves entities,
normalizes line endings, or mutates input. Every span is a half-open byte range
into the exact original UTF-8 input; attribute value and comment/PI/text/CDATA
content spans exclude their delimiters. QName `prefix` is empty when absent;
`local_name` is always populated. Namespaces are not resolved. Token data is
valid only while the caller's input remains alive and unchanged.

The scanner is iterative, linear in input length plus the bounded attribute
and name comparisons, and uses a fixed 256-entry element-name stack. Duplicate
attribute detection compares prior attribute tokens for the current element,
so the worst case is quadratic in attributes on that element. No recursion or
heap allocation occurs. On any failure `token_count` and success counts are
zero and `diagnostic` contains a stable category and an offset in `[0,input.len]`.
Output exhaustion is an ordinary diagnostic.

Defaults are 16 MiB input, 256 nested elements, 1,000,000 nodes,
4,096 attributes per element, 1,000,000 attributes total, and 4 MiB per
character-data or CDATA run. Names are additionally capped at 4,096 UTF-8
bytes as a fixed implementation bound. The caller can lower each configurable
cap but cannot raise it; depth cannot exceed the fixed 256-entry stack. A node is an
element, comment, PI, in-element text run, or CDATA run. XML declaration is
not a node. Whitespace outside the document element is tokenized but does not
count as a node.

`svg_xml_tokenize_large` uses the same grammar, token layout, and non-input
limits while permitting a source up to 1 GiB. It still writes into caller-owned
token storage and reports output exhaustion normally. The bounded index module
uses it on a validation worker; this does not change the 16 MiB cap or
allocation-free behavior of `svg_xml_tokenize`.

`svg_xml_token_stream` is the resumable full-token scanner for sources up to
1 GiB. It borrows immutable source bytes, checks XML characters incrementally,
and emits one-shot-equivalent token records across bounded calls. Its owned
token vector grows only within the caller's byte budget; `take` transfers the
completed vector, while `destroy` frees any vector not transferred. Cancellation
is checked during character scanning and parsing. A failed stream exposes its
stable diagnostic but cannot transfer a partial token vector. The index uses
this API on its worker so `token_at` data is produced by resumable scanning,
independently of the owner's progressive element reader.
Long text, comment, CDATA, and processing-instruction runs retain their scan
cursor across steps; the C regression test compares these token spans against
the one-shot tokenizer while checking the byte budget on every step.
`svg_xml_token_stream_bytes_read` reports the grammar-parser frontier (after
character validation) so other threads can safely determine whether an early
source span has been validated. If validation fails, the error offset bounds
which earlier spans remain valid.
`svg_xml_token_stream_start_visitor` provides discard-mode delivery. It keeps
fixed scanner state plus scratch for one element (one start token and at most
4,096 attribute tokens), then calls the visitor with the finalized start or
empty-element token followed by its attributes in source order. Thus token
scratch is bounded independently of document token count. Other token kinds
are delivered after validation. Callback spans borrow immutable source bytes;
the caller must keep the input alive and unchanged through stream destruction.
Returning false from a callback cancels delivery. Earlier callbacks can have
occurred when later input fails, so only `SVG_XML_STREAM_COMPLETE` means the
entire document validated. `svg_xml_token_stream_visitor_storage_bytes` reports
the fixed per-element scratch allocation.

`svg_xml_decode_attribute_value` decodes predefined and decimal/hexadecimal
numeric XML references into caller-owned UTF-8 storage. It does not expand
custom entities or resolve external resources. On failure it reports the
offending byte offset relative to the supplied raw attribute span; output
capacity is checked before every write.

`svg_xml_reader` is a resumable source scanner for large documents. It borrows
the immutable source, retains lexical state across calls, and advances no more
than the requested budget (capped at 64 KiB). It emits complete element tag
spans as they become available; comments, CDATA, and processing instructions
are skipped while preserving their boundary state. The reader remains separate
from the full-token stream so the owner can index element spans without waiting
for grammar validation. Consumers must not treat early tag events as proof
that the whole input is valid. Name bytes above ASCII are passed through for
the token stream to check against XML 1.0 Name rules.

Accepted syntax includes XML 1.0 documents encoded as UTF-8 with an optional
leading BOM, XML declaration,
PI, comments, element and empty-element tags, quoted attributes, character
data, and CDATA. Predefined and numeric references are retained lexically;
custom entity references are rejected because DTDs are unsupported. A single
`<!DOCTYPE>` before the root element, with or without an internal subset, is
skipped unprocessed and emitted as one `SVG_XML_TOKEN_DOCTYPE` token whose
source span covers the declaration (`xml_doctype.h` holds the shared skipper);
no entity is declared or expanded, so a reference to a non-predefined entity
still fails as malformed syntax. A DOCTYPE after the root, a second DOCTYPE and
a bare `<!ENTITY` are still rejected. No namespace URI
resolution, DTD, external entity, serializer, or tree is provided. XML 1.0
character and Name character ranges are validated; encoding declarations must
say UTF-8. Line endings and entity spellings are never normalized.
# SVG shape decoding

The shape module turns borrowed SVG bytes and XML tokens into owned flattened
edges, per-shape fill and stroke state, gradients, clips, and opacity groups.
`traverse.c` owns bounded token traversal and inherited contexts;
`traverse_use.c` resolves live `<use>` instances. `transform.c` parses affine
transforms; `shape_path.c` decodes paths and `shape_geometry.c` decodes basic geometry; `shape_custom.c`
shares style, paint, stroke, and clip setup with text/image geometry. `text.c`
lays out text runs, `text_cache.c` bounds and owns shaped runs, and `image.c`
decodes embedded data through the injected provider. `viewport.c` resolves root,
nested `<svg>`, and symbol viewports; `document.c` owns public cleanup and
`selection.c` provides editor mapping, bounds, and hit tests.

`svg_shape_decode` also attaches a bounded, source-backed SMIL model on
`svg_shape_document.animation`. Animation elements are omitted from static
traversal while their target/keyframe source spans and stable diagnostics stay
available for timeline enumeration and explicit-time evaluation.

Traversal records a parent-linked transform frame for each rendered instance.
Frames keep the authored transform separate from `<use>`/symbol placement and
nested viewport mapping, so animation evaluation can replace or compose a
local transform without flattening away its ancestors. Frame indices are
instance-specific even when several `<use>` elements render the same source
element. Decoded source bytes and the static geometry remain unchanged.

Supported geometry includes all SVG path commands (`M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z`,
absolute and relative), `<line>`, `<polyline>`, `<polygon>`, `<circle>`,
`<ellipse>`, and `<rect>`. Paths retain subpath and closed-stroke metadata so
strokes support caps, joins, miter limits, dash arrays, and dash offsets.
Rounded rectangles implement the `rx`/`ry` copy rule, radius clamping, and
elliptical corners. Curves are flattened with a transformed 0.25-unit tolerance
and a recursion cap of 16. Paths are limited to 65,536 commands and documents
to 262,144 edges.

Path operands may be separated by whitespace, commas, an explicit sign, or an
adjacent decimal point when the previous numeric token has already ended; for
example, `M-.4.6` means the points `(-0.4, 0.6)`. The decoder retains the exact
source and each numeric literal's original byte span instead of normalizing the
path text.

Transforms include matrix, translate, scale, rotate (including a center point),
`skewX`, and `skewY`. The paint CSS cascade covers fill/stroke rules, color and
opacity properties, visibility, display, clips, and gradient stops. The shared
color parser accepts 148 named colors, `rgb()`/`rgba()`/`hsl()`/`hsla()`, 3/4/6/8
digit hex, `transparent`, and context-resolved `currentColor`. Selectors allow
up to four descendant terms and sixteen class terms per term. Child/sibling,
pseudo, attribute, namespace, at-rule, and resource selectors remain unsupported.

Root and nested `<svg>` viewports support viewBox transforms and
`preserveAspectRatio` alignment, `meet`, `slice`, and `none`. Nested viewports
clip their descendants. Shape lengths accept percentages and `px`, `pt`, `mm`,
`cm`, `in`, and `em`; `em` currently resolves to 16 user units and does not
compute inherited `font-size` outside text layout. Fill/stroke opacity and
isolated element/group opacity are supported. Opacity group rendering uses
bounded tile scratch and returns `limit` if nested layers exceed 64 MiB.

An additive media-aware entry point accepts injected text and image providers;
the core decoder does not link to platform frameworks. `<text>` and `<tspan>`
inherit font family, size, weight, style, anchor, and spacing from the CSS
cascade. They accept x/y/dx/dy coordinate lists, decode the five XML named
entities and numeric entities, collapse whitespace by default, and honor
`xml:space="preserve"`. CoreText glyph outlines are converted into the regular
shape edge pipeline. Text is capped at 64 KiB, 16,384 glyphs, and 262,144
provider path commands per document; repeated identical runs use a bounded
decode-local cache. `<textPath>` returns a stable unsupported diagnostic.

`<image>` accepts strict Base64 `data:image/png` and `data:image/jpeg` URIs,
local x/y/width/height, transforms, opacity, clip paths, and
`preserveAspectRatio` meet/slice/none. The injected ImageIO provider decodes
premultiplied RGBA with a 32 MiB encoded-input cap and a 64-million-pixel
aggregate budget per document. The scalar rasterizer samples bilinearly.
External image references and SVG data URIs remain unsupported; no filesystem
or network resource is loaded.

Each rendered shape carries its borrowed-source element byte range and
transform. Additive queries expose user-space and device-space bounds, resolve
a source byte offset to the most specific rendered element, and hit-test in
reverse paint order with fill, stroke tolerance, and clip membership. Every
decoded path also retains command-group and numeric-literal byte spans for
node-editing correspondence. The source bytes remain borrowed and unchanged.

`<defs>`, `<title>`, `<desc>`, `<metadata>`, and Inkscape's
`sodipodi:namedview` are non-rendering; metadata subtrees are structurally
tokenized and then skipped. Unknown prefixed export attributes are ignored
without changing their borrowed source bytes. `<meta>`, a `<!DOCTYPE>`
(never expanded), `writing-mode` and unknown non-namespaced attributes that are
not SVG rendering attributes are also ignored for rendering (ADR-0016 decision
5). `svg_shape_document.ignored[]` records a count and first byte offset per
kind, and `render-frame` prints one `note: ignored <kind> xN, first at byte M`
line per kind on success. Known rendering attributes the decoder does not
support still fail closed. `<symbol>` is
non-rendering unless reached by a live `<use>`. Local `href="#id"` and
root-bound `xlink:href="#id"` references
traverse the original token array at the use position. The ID table supports up
to 65,536 unique IDs; reference depth is capped at 16, instances at 65,536,
each referenced span at 64 KiB, and aggregate span visits at 1 MiB. Diagnostics
keep offsets into the original borrowed source.

Clip paths support local references, `userSpaceOnUse` or `objectBoundingBox`,
and unions of up to 64 basic shape/path children. Group/use clips use their
subtree AABB. Nested clip declarations inside clip geometry and external
references fail closed. Raster work, clip geometry, stylesheet data, and
references retain their fixed budgets; unsupported XML/CSS semantics return
stable diagnostics rather than dropping source or fetching resources.
Local `<clipPath>` definitions are skipped as non-rendering content wherever
they appear in the SVG tree, while remaining available for local reference
resolution when nested outside `<defs>`. The inherited SVG `clip-rule` property
is applied to geometry inside the referenced clip path through the supported
CSS cascade; it does not inherit from the drawable that references the clip.

The deterministic scalar 4×4 rasterizer is compared with librsvg using small
fixtures. Text uses structural, ink-bound, and ink-area tolerances because
CoreText and Pango may resolve different sans-serif faces and rasterize glyph
edges differently. This is selected-feature differential evidence, not full
SVG parity.
SVG semantics follow W3C SVG 2 Shapes, Paths, CSS, Paint Servers, Document
Structure, and Clipping specs (consulted 2026-10-09). No SVG editor source is
used.

## W5 paint servers and effects

The decoder also resolves local `<mask>`, `<pattern>`, `<marker>`, and
`<filter>` references. Masks support alpha and luminance sampling, both mask
coordinate systems, and nested local masks. Patterns support fill and stroke
paint, user-space and object-bounding-box units, content units, transforms,
viewBox mapping, and repeat tiling from a decode-local RGBA tile cache. Marker
start, mid, and end positions work on paths, lines, polylines, and polygons;
`marker` shorthand, stroke-width or user-space sizing, `auto`,
`auto-start-reverse`, numeric orientation, reference points, and marker viewBox
mapping are included.

Local linear and radial gradients are supported on fills and strokes, including
gradient stop opacity and stroke opacity. Gradient strokes use the same
document-space center sampling as gradient fills; unresolved and unsupported
paint-server references fail with a source diagnostic.

Default solid fills and strokes do not allocate a full paint-server record per
shape; the decoder keeps compact per-shape indices and stores only non-default
fill and stroke paints. Dash descriptors store an offset/count, and values are
kept in a bounded document array only for strokes that specify a dash pattern;
the per-pattern maximum remains 16 values. The shape-count ceiling remains
65,536; remaining large-document metadata costs and process RSS still require
measurement.

Filters support bounded `feGaussianBlur`, `feOffset`, `feFlood`, `feBlend`,
`feComposite`, `feMerge`, `feColorMatrix`, and `feDropShadow` chains. Filter
and primitive units, regions, named results, `SourceGraphic`, `SourceAlpha`,
and `color-interpolation-filters` (`linearRGB` or `sRGB`) are handled. Stable
named unsupported diagnostics cover turbulence, displacement, convolution,
image, lighting, and morphology primitives. CSS blending supports normal,
multiply, screen, darken, and lighten with isolated groups. `<switch>` selects
the first supported `systemLanguage` child; the default language is `en`, and
`svg_shape_decode_with_system_language` injects another bounded tag. `<a>` is a
pass-through container. Existing `<symbol>` viewBox traversal also accepts
the W5 paint properties.

The CSS cascade recognizes 39 properties, including W5 effects, markers,
masking, blending, paint order, shape rendering, and vector effects. Crisp-edge
rendering uses the deterministic center sample. Non-scaling strokes currently
support uniform affine and viewport scales. `stroke-linejoin: arcs` and
`miter-clip` use stable round and miter fallbacks.

Definitions and scratch stay bounded: masks, patterns, and markers cap
instances at 1,024 per decode; pattern tiles cap each axis at 4,096 pixels, each tile at 1,048,576
pixels, and aggregate retained tiles at 16 MiB. Mask, pattern, and marker
recursion is capped at eight. Filter chains cap at 16 primitives, merges at
eight inputs, 50 million pixel-primitive work units, and 64 MiB of filter
scratch. Isolated group scratch remains capped at 64 MiB. Cycles and exhausted
limits fail with stable diagnostics. External filter, mask, pattern, and marker
references are not loaded.
# SVG paint servers

This module resolves bounded local linear and radial gradients used by a
shape's computed fill. The stop array belongs to the decoded shape document;
the temporary definition cache is destroyed during decode cleanup. Sampling is
deterministic in the scalar rasterizer and maps pixel coordinates back through
the referencing element's inverse transform. `objectBoundingBox` coordinates
use the element's untransformed local bounds.

Local `<pattern>` fills and strokes are resolved by the sibling shape pattern
module. Each definition is rendered once into a bounded RGBA tile and cached
for the decode; the paint sampler repeats that tile after its unit, content,
viewBox, and transform mappings.

The shape paint tag also has an image variant. Embedded image storage and URI
validation belong to shape decoding; raster image sampling is handled by
`src/raster/shape_render_sample.c`, not by this gradient resolver.

Linear and radial gradients support 2–256 monotone finite stops, stop opacity,
`objectBoundingBox` and `userSpaceOnUse`, and `pad`, `reflect`, or `repeat`
spread. Invertible affine `gradientTransform` values are supported. Radial
gradients accept `fx`/`fy`; omitted focal coordinates follow the resolved
`cx`/`cy`. Gradient attributes inherit through local `href="#id"` and bound
`xlink:href="#id"` chains up to 16 definitions. A child gradient's stops take
precedence; otherwise stops come from the nearest referenced gradient with
stops.

Stop colors use the shared CSS parser (148 names, RGB/HSL functions, alpha hex,
`transparent`, and `currentColor`) and CSS cascade for presentation attributes,
inline styles, and supported selectors. `currentColor` follows inherited
`color`, defaulting to black. An omitted `stop-color` defaults to black. Stops
are limited to 65,536 total per document; referenced definitions are cached in
a fixed 65,536-slot table with at most 32,768 entries. Cache keys include the
active viewport dimensions because percentage coordinates vary by viewport.
The gradient parser has a 4,194,304-token visit budget.

User-space coordinate percentages resolve against the active root or nested
viewport. Lengths accept unitless values and `px`, `pt`, `mm`, `cm`, `in`, and
`em` (`em` is 16 user units in the current subset). Unsupported gradient types,
external URLs, malformed chains, cycles, noninvertible transforms, invalid
stops, and unsupported CSS declarations fail with stable diagnostics. No
external resource is loaded.
# Scalar shape rasterizer

`raster_shape_render` allocates a caller-owned transparent RGBA tile and fills
the flattened edges from `svg_shape_document`. Geometry remains in user space;
the root viewBox maps it to the tile with the parsed `preserveAspectRatio`
alignment and `meet`, `slice`, or `none` behavior. The default is centered
`xMidYMid meet`. Nested `<svg>` viewport clips are carried by the shape
document. Each pixel uses a deterministic 4x4 grid at offsets
`{0.125, 0.375, 0.625, 0.875}` on each axis. For each shape, a sample is
covered only when it is inside the shape and inside every clip in its chain.
Pixel coverage is the rounded fraction of those 16 covered samples. A gradient
is evaluated once at the pixel center, and that color is used for every
covered sample; translucent gradient samples keep source-over compositing.
Final RGB is averaged over nontransparent sample colors and alpha is averaged
across all 16 samples. Fully covered opaque pixels retain the exact paint color
and empty pixels stay transparent black. Edges are grouped by source element,
fill rules are evaluated per element, and later painted elements replace
earlier opaque fills at each subpixel before coverage is resolved. A
`fill="none"` element is parsed but does not erase earlier pixels. The output
tile must be empty when passed in.

`raster_shape_render_at` evaluates the document's bounded SMIL overlay at a
caller-supplied time. It clones the mutable geometry/color/stroke/transform
arrays needed for that frame, leaves source and decoded arrays unchanged, and
reuses the regular deterministic scalar renderer. Each rendered element has a
bounded transform-frame chain, including the authored transform, `<use>` or
symbol placement, and nested viewport mapping. Animated transforms replace the
authored transform by default, `additive="sum"` post-composes, and multiple
transform tracks compose in document order. Motion and numeric geometry are
applied in the target's user space before the same ancestor chain. Object-box
gradient bounds and per-instance clip transforms/bounds are refreshed on the
overlay; shared decoded clips are copied within a 64 MiB frame cap. Animated
path morphing returns `unsupported` because the scene stores flattened path
edges. Geometry or transform animation inside a filtered or masked opacity
group also returns `unsupported`; those effects need their own animated
coordinate update.

Embedded PNG/JPEG image fills sample provider-owned premultiplied RGBA8 with
bilinear interpolation in inverse-transformed local coordinates. Sampling is
bounded by the image viewport, source pixel dimensions, and clip chain; image
opacity is applied through the same isolated opacity groups as vector content.
Text reaches this renderer as flattened CoreText outline edges, so fill/stroke,
clips, transforms, and opacity follow the regular shape path.

After each element's fill, bounded strokes are tested against the same 4x4
sample grid. The stroke decoder stores each element's ordered edge range,
literal RGBA color, local width, inverse element transform, cap/join policy,
and bounded dash state.
Before rasterization, stroke intervals and joins are materialized once. A
conservative local-space grid narrows each sample to nearby stroke pieces;
segments include cap reach and joins include the miter-limit reach. Grid cells
are at least 1 user unit wide, each axis is at most 128 cells, and all shapes
share caps of 65,536 cells, 1,000,000 references, and 16 MiB of cache storage.
The dash builder is capped at 65,536 pieces per array and 1,000,000 build steps.
If a shape cannot be indexed within those bounds, it uses the bounded linear
stroke scan and the work preflight accounts for every piece tested. The
preflight also charges grid lookups and candidate pieces per sample, so sparse
paths no longer pay for every edge inside the path's full bounding rectangle.
The renderer computes a conservative device-space box for each shape's fill and
stroke. Stroke boxes include the transformed half-width, miter-limit reach,
square-cap reach, and a small floating-point margin. The box maps to every tile
pixel that can contain one of the 4x4 sample points. Empty and zero-area
geometry stays harmless; invalid or non-finite bounds conservatively select
the full tile. The one-bit boundary map marks pixels near every painted-shape
edge, with stroke reach included, and every clip child edge in each clipped
shape's full parent chain. Clip geometry is mapped through its element
transform into device space; object-bounding-box clip edges are first mapped
through the painted shape bounds. Edge boxes expand beyond the 4x4 sample
footprint to stay conservative. The center-sample fast path is used only
outside this map and outside partial viewport pixels, where no shape or clip
edge can cross the pixel. Gradient interior variation does not require marking
because gradient color is sampled at the pixel center.

Shapes are visited in source paint order and only over their clipped boxes.
A y-interval event set yields the shapes whose bounds intersect the current
row, avoiding a full shape-list scan for every tile row. A scanline event table
maintains each shape's fill edges whose half-open y-range contains each sample
row. The active set is emitted in original edge order;
the crossing arithmetic, winding/parity updates, color replacement, stroke
tests, sample locations, and final RGBA rounding keep the reference operation
order. The test-only `raster_shape_render_reference` has no boundary map or
center shortcut: it tests all 16 sample positions for every pixel against
every shape and clip, while evaluating gradient paint at the pixel center. It
serves as the byte-comparison oracle for production culling and scanline paths.

The renderer rejects invalid viewport data, malformed edge/group arrays, and
actual post-culling work above the existing 200,000,000-operation cap. The
checked work estimate includes tile pixels, summed shape-box pixels, painted
and clip edge boundary-map visits and pixel marks, scanline events and
active-edge visits, fill crossings, gradient-stop and clip-test work, and
stroke edge/dash work for each relevant sample. Checked arithmetic rejects overflow
and excessive work before rendering; quality is never reduced to satisfy the
cap. Temporary storage is bounded by shape/edge counts, tile dimensions, and
the output tile: the boundary map is one bit per tile pixel, sample buffers are
one row wide, and scanline events are at most two per edge. Rendering remains
single-threaded and deterministic. Output ownership
passes to the caller only on success, who releases it with `raster_tile_destroy`.

Element/group `opacity` is composited in isolated RGBA layers after the group
contents have painted. Nested layers composite source-over in document order.
Scratch tile bytes are checked and capped at 64 MiB; a request above the cap
returns a limit diagnostic instead of painting a partial frame.

## Raster modules

- `shape_render.c` validates the document, builds bounds and scanline state,
  enforces the existing checked work cap, and coordinates deterministic sample
  traversal and RGBA output.
- `shape_render_sample.c` evaluates one fill sample, applies clip membership and
  paint-server sampling, then composites the fill and stroke with the existing
  integer source-over operation. It preserves the test-only scalar alpha mode.
- `shape_render_stroke.c` materializes local stroke segments and tests caps,
  joins, miter limits, dash intervals, and closed-path dash seams.
- `shape_render_stroke_grid.c` builds and queries the bounded local-space stroke
  grid; the scalar reference remains an unindexed comparison path.
- `shape_render_group.c` renders isolated opacity subtrees using bounded tile
  scratch and composites each layer with source-over alpha.
- `shape_bounds.c` owns conservative device-space shape boxes and the boundary
  mask; `shape_scanline.c` owns row events and active-edge ordering.
- `shape_render_internal.h` carries private measurement and helper contracts;
  the public `shape_render.h` API is unchanged.

## Tile cache

`raster_tile_cache` is mutable from one owner thread and has no platform or shape-decoding dependencies. Its explicit byte cap is nonzero and at most 256 MiB. Accounted bytes include the complete preallocated entry array and every occupied tile's RGBA payload; creation rejects a slot array larger than the cap. LRU ties use stable slot order; a two-part monotonic tick preserves recency across tick rollover. Cache keys are caller supplied. Changing generation or integer scale bucket through `raster_tile_cache_set_epoch` clears all entries. A successful put transfers the tile's malloc-owned RGBA allocation and clears the caller's tile; a failed put leaves the caller's tile owned and unchanged. Lookup returns a borrowed tile valid until the next cache call that mutates LRU/cache state or destruction.

Filter primitives run in bounded RGBA surfaces inside isolated group layers.
Gaussian blur uses separable finite kernels; offsets, flood, blend, composite,
merge, color matrix, and drop shadow keep deterministic scalar channel
rounding. `linearRGB` input is converted from sRGB before primitives and
converted back afterward; `sRGB` bypasses that conversion. Filter evaluation
is capped at 50 million pixel-primitive work units and 64 MiB of scratch, in
addition to the enclosing group layer's 64 MiB budget. W5 effect fixtures
compare selected output with `rsvg-convert`.
# Source-backed SVG index

The index session borrows an immutable complete byte slice until destruction.
`svg_index_step` examines no more than the requested budget, capped at 64 KiB.
Element and name ranges refer directly to that slice; no source text is copied.
Mutable session state belongs to one owner thread. Cancellation and generation
changes are also owner-thread operations. A canceled session cannot be resumed.

The large-input path has independent limits (1 GiB source, depth 256, one
million elements and attributes, and 256 MiB combined element-record and
token-vector capacity (each vector is capped at half that budget). Index
records are owner-thread-only. A bounded task validates the complete source
with the same XML grammar and exposes its token spans after completion; worker
allocations are capped before retrying token output. The existing one-shot
tokenizer remains capped at 16 MiB and its defaults do not change.

Once a supported depth-one shape has a complete source range and the background
token stream has validated all bytes through that range, `first_preview_ready`
becomes true. The owner pauses element scanning while that prefix validation
catches up. An error before or inside the candidate span blocks publication; a
later malformed tail still allows the already validated preview while the
session reports failure. `svg_index_make_preview_source` returns an owned
minimal SVG consisting of the original root opener and shape span. Callers
schedule decode/raster work and must retain that owned byte buffer through task
completion.

The early preview subset requires an SVG root with supported `width` and
`height` attributes and an unprefixed `rect` or `path` whose attribute names
are accepted by the current shape decoder. Unsupported attributes such as
`transform`, element prefixes, and unsupported root attributes keep the source
record but mark it unsupported, allowing a later eligible shape to be chosen.
Start tags longer than 64 KiB remain indexed with their original spans but are
not scanned for early-preview eligibility; this keeps owner-thread attribute
inspection within the step budget. The UI marks a preview visible only after
the worker has produced its owned raster tile.
# SVG SMIL animation model

`smil.c` reads bounded animation values and simple timing controls;
`smil_tracks.c` associates supported animation elements with their target spans;
`motion_path.c` resolves local `<mpath>` references and flattens the line-only
motion-path subset; `evaluate.c` samples timing and interpolation without
changing source bytes. `svg_shape_document.animation` owns the track/keyframe
arrays and borrows every value and source span from `document.source`.

The model accepts up to 128 tracks, 256 key values per track, 128 stable
diagnostics, and a one-hour document timeline. It supports numeric geometry and
opacity properties, literal solid `fill`/`stroke` colors, `<set>`, the
`translate`/`scale`/`rotate`/`skewX`/`skewY` transform types, simple offset and
syncbase begin/end timing, repeat count/duration, `remove`/`freeze`, key times,
linear/spline/discrete/paced interpolation, and additive/accumulate for numeric
and color values. Motion paths accept local `path` or `mpath` references made
from one `M` plus `L`, `H`, `V`, and `Z` segments, with numeric, `auto`, and
`auto-reverse` rotation.

Event timing, CSS animation/transition rules, external motion references,
curved/arc motion paths, and malformed or over-limit tracks produce stable
diagnostic kinds and byte offsets. `<animate attributeName="d">` is parsed only
when each key has the same path command/number structure; the current raster
overlay reports it unsupported because changing flattened curve topology is
not yet implemented. The renderer applies numeric and color overlays to leaf
shapes and composes transform/motion overlays through a bounded per-render-
instance ancestry chain. This includes groups, `<use>`/symbol placement, and
nested viewport mappings; animated transform replacement and additive sum are
kept distinct, and multiple transform tracks compose in document order.
Object-box gradients and clips update with animated bounds. Filtered/masked
opacity groups, active path morphing, geometry changes under patterns, and
group opacity animation still return stable unsupported results when their
flattened scene data cannot represent the update.

## Source authoring

authoring.c builds byte patches for supported SMIL values, key timing, and
easing. The patch owns its replacement buffer; its source is borrowed from the
decoded animation document until the patch has been built. Callers apply the
single patch with document_edit_replace_source_span, then destroy it.

Only bounded numeric, supported color, and transform animate /
animateTransform tracks with finite simple timing and no additive,
accumulated, sync-base, paced, path, or motion semantics are editable. A
property-value edit rewrites only the animation start tag, preserving all
unrelated tag bytes and every byte outside that tag. Key sequences are capped
at 256 values, tags and individual values at 64 KiB, and one patch at 1 MiB.
Rejected and no-op operations produce no patch. Easing handles are finite and
in [0,1]; an interval edit preserves the raw text of other spline tuples.

Spline tracks accept key edits and keep exactly key_count-1 keySplines tuples,
passing each tuple's raw bytes through unchanged. A value edit or key move
keeps all tuples. Adding a key splits an interval and repeats that interval's
tuple. Deleting key 0 drops tuple 0, the last key drops the last tuple, and any
other key k drops tuple k. Deleting a spline track down to one key removes
keySplines and sets calcMode="linear", because a one-key spline track does not
parse. A keySplines or values result over 64 KiB returns the limit error before
any patch exists. Tuples are copied raw, so whitespace padding the parser
trims can make the output exceed 64 KiB (an add_key that duplicates a padded
tuple); the edge test covers this limit path. authoring_create.c holds track creation; both files share
authoring_internal.h.

Track creation returns one bounded animate fragment with explicit initial
and authored values, begin="0s", finite duration, and linear interpolation.
The editor inserts/removes it with the document edit transaction API. The
caller supplies the selected property's current typed value as the time-zero
seed; static field edits never call this module implicitly.
# 02 — Architecture

## Layers and dependency direction

```text
app / command registry
  ├─ ui_widgets → ui_core → accessibility snapshot
  ├─ editor → doc/edit/undo → svg_parse + svg_style + scene + spatial
  ├─ scene → raster → tile cache → platform.gfx → Metal texture blit
  └─ platform services: window/input/IME/clipboard/dialog/text/menu/a11y
base ← all portable modules; OS modules never leak into portable headers
```

Portable C17 modules may depend only downward. `platform` implements opaque interfaces and may call `base`; `app` composes all. Rendering consumes immutable `scene_frame` snapshots. UI does not reach into SVG parser structs. No module includes another module's private header.

## Public API sketches

Header sketches are contracts, not final ABI. Keep public types opaque except small value structs. Each API returns status; no hidden global error.

# 03 — SVG parsing, large files, round-trip (Q5, Q8)

## Storage architecture

Use `mmap`/read-only mapping on platforms where available, but allow a streaming fallback. Keep original UTF-8 byte buffer immutable for the lifetime of a document; parser indexes token/source spans into it. Do not mutate mapped bytes. Build compact node/attribute arrays in arenas, not one malloc per XML item:

```c
typedef struct { uint32_t off, len; } StrSpan;       // bytes in source or intern table
typedef struct { uint32_t parent, first_child, next_sibling;
                 uint32_t name_id, attr_begin, attr_count;
                 uint32_t src_begin, src_end, flags; } XmlNode;
typedef struct { uint32_t name_id; StrSpan value; } XmlAttr;
```

Store nodes/attrs in chunked SoA or compact arrays; retain original spans and namespace-qualified names. Intern frequent element/attribute names, but avoid interning arbitrary long text/path strings. Parse path/style/transform/length values lazily and cache decoded data by node generation. Build scene nodes only for renderable/interactive content; keep unsupported subtree opaque. Add strict depth/entity/resource limits; disable external entities and remote-resource loads by default.

### Parser design choices

- Single pass XML tokenizer: quote-aware tag boundary scanning, UTF-8 validation, comments/CDATA/PI/DOCTYPE handling per explicit policy; record token/source spans, stack parent indices, namespace declarations. SVG files generally need namespace handling; namespace prefixes are arbitrary.
- A SIMD “structural index” stage can accelerate scanning for `<`, `>`, quotes, `&`, whitespace, but JSON simdjson speeds are **not transferable to XML**. XML nesting, quoted delimiters, entities and UTF encodings change the problem. Benchmark an ASCII fast path with scalar correctness fallback.
- Streaming parse and mmap are not mutually exclusive: map input, parse while building compact arrays, free decoded transient data; progressive scene compile can begin once a subtree is closed. Large root-level siblings can render before EOF if the format is not malformed.
- Avoid full generic DOM. pugixml documents a markup-heavy 2.1 MB sample using 2.1 MB source buffer + 8.3 MB document structures on 64-bit; it also offers a more compact mode with speed tradeoff. [pugixml manual](https://pugixml.org/docs/manual.html) Its parser comparison uses 1–20 MB files and minimum repeated parse time, not 500 MB SVG editor sessions. [benchmark](https://pugixml.org/benchmark.html)
- simdjson reports GB/s on JSON and explains allocation can dominate (their docs mention ~1.4 GB/s allocation behavior on some systems); use as motivation to reduce allocations, not an SVG/XML performance claim. [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson) · [performance notes](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson/blob/master/doc/performance.md)
- Native XML libraries: Expat SAX, libxml2, pugixml, RapidXML, yxml differ in validation/DOM/encoding/support. If strict no-vendor means own parser, still use differential fuzzing against multiple established parsers. Do not claim a parse GB/s target until measured on actual SVG fixtures.

## CSS and SVG subset

Implement the highest-value static subset in explicit phases:

1. Presentation attributes + inline style declarations; property tables; inherited properties/defaults; `currentColor`, `inherit`, opacity, fill/stroke, stroke width/cap/join/miter, fill-rule, display/visibility, font basics.
2. `<style>` blocks with tokenizer/declaration parser; selectors: type, universal, class, ID, descendant/child, comma lists, supported pseudo-classes as documented. Specificity sort + source order. Unsupported selectors are preserved and flagged.
3. CSS variables/custom properties and `var()` resolution after cascade, with cycle detection; CSS units/font-relative units and viewport percentages resolved against context.
4. Transform lists, viewBox/preserveAspectRatio, nested `<svg>`, `symbol` and `use` references with cycle/depth guards; paint servers gradients and stop styles.
5. ClipPath, masks, patterns, markers. Then filters (blur, offset, color matrix, composite/blend) with bounded offscreen regions. External image links optional and explicit; no scripting/foreignObject in MVP.

For path data, one tokenizer must correctly handle sign-separated floats (`10-3`), exponents, omitted commas, repeated command parameters, smooth control points, arc flags and close-path. Parse relative coordinates while carrying current point/subpath origin. Use locale-independent float parse (C `strtod` is locale-sensitive and often slow); writing can use a shortest-round-trip algorithm such as Ryu. Eisel-Lemire-style fast parsing may be adapted, but no maintained canonical C implementation specifically for SVG was established here. Unknown: relative speed across target CPUs.

## 500 MB / 1 GB strategy

File size is a poor proxy. A file of long path numbers can have modest node count; base64 images can dominate bytes and decoded RAM; a million tiny elements can make indexes dominate. Track both encoded and expanded size.

- Document state: immutable mapped/original byte store; compact token arrays; scene-index pages allocated on demand; no per-element heap object. Report estimated bytes per XML node after prototype; do not predeclare a realistic number without profiling.
- Loading: parse in worker; publish completed subtrees; display progress and first viewport as soon as viewBox and visible scene bounds are available. When global styles or `<use>` dependencies arrive later, invalidate affected nodes.
- Spatial index: R-tree/BVH over conservative object bounds; separate layers/order index for painter’s order; special dependency graph for clip/mask/pattern/use. Build lazily and incrementally. Avoid index work for offscreen giant documents until needed.
- Rendering: visible tiles + LOD by zoom. At low zoom replace dense groups with cached tile/simplified geometry; preserve exact geometry at high zoom/selection. Screen-space simplification is render-only. Tile cache uses a memory budget and LRU; cancel stale pan/zoom jobs.
- Editing: document edits produce operations and local bounds invalidation; don't rebuild whole scene. A huge single path still requires full path parse for editing; tokenize path subranges or make parse cancellable. Render coarse preview while decode proceeds.
- Save: patch dirty spans when structural conditions permit; otherwise serialize changed subtrees and preserve untouched bytes. Atomic temp-write + rename; autosave operation log and recovery checkpoint.
- Very large untrusted inputs: configurable memory cap, maximum recursion/reference chain/filter extent, graceful “partial viewer” mode, no external entity expansion/network fetch.

## Round-trip, undo and recovery

Preserve source spans for untouched nodes; dirty flags identify exact start/end ranges. If edits alter one attribute, rewrite the start tag while preserving other attribute order/quotes where practical; if namespaces, inherited CSS or child order are touched, reserialize that subtree. Guarantee semantic preservation first; byte-identical output for untouched spans second. Track namespace bindings and original encodings/newlines. Build corpus assertions that unknown nodes, metadata, comments, IDs, styles, and editor namespaces survive open/save.

Undo/redo is an operation log, not whole-document copies: each operation stores stable node ID, before/after values or geometry, inverse, source spans and generation. Allocate undo records from chunked arenas; checkpoints bound replay. Autosave uses periodic compacted snapshots plus log; recovery scans valid records after crash. Keep save-as and source file backups explicit. Animation later attaches tracks to stable IDs and maps tracks to SMIL/CSS output; app-private namespace only for metadata not representable in standards. Round-trip private attributes unchanged.

# 02 — Rasterization and text (Q3, Q4)

## Renderer decision

**Recommendation:** own an SVG-aware scene compiler and tiled CPU rasterizer first; use Metal as a presentation/upload path. Keep `RasterBackend` swappable. A C CPU rasterizer offers deterministic output, easy test capture, and no GPU driver dependency; it is a good first viewport renderer, but it is not automatically fastest for every zoom level. Add Metal acceleration only when measurement shows rasterization, not parse/scene work, dominates. Do not begin by implementing general GPU path rendering.

### CPU design

1. Convert SVG path commands to canonical cubic/line geometry; flatten curves adaptively to screen-space tolerance (e.g. 0.25 px), preserve exact source commands for edit/save.
2. For each path, clip transformed bounds to visible tiles; build monotone edges and scan-convert with analytic area/coverage accumulation per pixel. Use winding counts for nonzero/even-odd fill. Avoid 4x supersampling as the default; reserve it for quality/debug comparisons.
3. Rasterize into 128–256 px tiles; parallelize independent tiles with bounded worker pool and immutable display-list snapshots. Keep tile cache keyed by transform/style/scale and invalidate changed bounds plus filter expansion.
4. Compose solid/linear/radial gradients, image patterns, opacity, clip paths, masks and Porter-Duff blend modes. Use premultiplied linear-light working colors where appropriate; explicitly test SVG color/compositing semantics.
5. Vectorize row coverage, span fills, color conversion and compositing using scalar baseline + dispatchable SSE2/AVX2/NEON. Keep intrinsics behind a small `simd.h`; compare exact/allowed output against scalar. Do not use SIMD where branch-heavy curve/clip setup dominates.
6. Filters are offscreen graph nodes with declared region, resolution and dependency expansion. Implement blur/offset/color matrix first; cap offscreen dimensions and expose fallback diagnostics.

### GPU path options

| Approach | Upside | Cost / recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| GPU compute path rasterization (Vello-like) | Scales coverage work across GPU, can merge many paths and compose in tiles | Complex shader/compiler, GPU resource lifetime, synchronization, driver variation, readback/testing, Metal-specific implementation; prototype after CPU baseline. |
| Stencil-and-cover | Mature path technique; GPU handles coverage and fill | Stencil complexity, path complexity and overdraw; API availability/platform correctness. Do not make first renderer. |
| Tessellate paths to triangles | Reuse conventional GPU pipelines; simple shapes fast | Robust curves/intersections/self-overlap are hard; triangle count and antialias seams; unsuitable as a universal fill engine. |
| MSDF / Slug-style text | Fast scalable glyph rendering with texture/analytic approaches | Text-only path; specialized implementation and licensing/evaluation required. Not SVG path renderer. |
| CPU tiles → GPU texture | Portable visual semantics, easy deterministic baseline, cheap Metal integration | Full viewport tile upload can be bandwidth-heavy; partial dirty rect uploads and double buffering. **Recommended M0/M1.** |

## Text strategy

“Own text” should mean owning editor layout/state and converting glyph outlines to the same display pipeline where possible, not implementing OpenType shaping from scratch.

| Option | What it gives | Cost / gaps |
|---|---|---|
| Own TrueType subset (`glyf`, `loca`, `cmap`, `head`, `hhea`, `hmtx`, `maxp`, `name`, basic variation later) | No runtime dependency; extract outlines/advances; small simple Latin subset possible | Font format security/parser burden, CFF/CFF2, variations, hinting, color fonts, TTC and licensing/document embedding issues. `stb_truetype` is a permissive single-header example; check current license/version. [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) |
| Own glyph outlines + own raster | One geometry path for SVG and text; consistent zoom/edit | No shaping: Arabic/Indic/SEA joining/reordering, ligatures, mark positioning, contextual forms and OpenType GPOS/GSUB fail; kerning only covers simple legacy `kern` if implemented. |
| System shaping: CoreText / DirectWrite / Linux font stack | Correct font fallback, shaping, metrics, IME integration; avoids embedding fonts | OS-dependent output and font metrics; need backend adapters and deterministic test font fixture. CoreText is Apple’s text framework [CoreText](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coretext); DirectWrite offers font/layout APIs [guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/directwrite/programming-guide). Linux usually needs fontconfig + FreeType + HarfBuzz, which are system deps or must be bundled. |
| HarfBuzz + FreeType bundled | Consistent shaping and broad formats on all OSes | Adds dependencies, build/size/license work; contrary to “own everything,” but cheapest parity path. [HarfBuzz](https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz) |

### Text MVP

- UI chrome: system shaping/text APIs, platform font fallback, baseline metrics and selection/caret/IME.
- SVG text read-only in M0: basic `font-family`, size, weight, anchor, x/y/dx/dy, spans and whitespace; preserve unknown text attributes. Draw shaped runs from OS API or cache glyph outlines where available.
- M2 editing: plain text and basic per-span style edits, OS-backed shaping, caret/selection, SVG `<text>/<tspan>` round-trip.
- Defer vertical writing, complex text-on-path fidelity, advanced OpenType features UI, variable/color fonts editing, embedded fonts, exact cross-platform pixel identity.

**System dependency recommendation:** Mac CoreText, Windows DirectWrite; Linux provisionally use `fontconfig + FreeType + HarfBuzz` (distro libraries) because there is no universal Linux system shaper equivalent. # Scalar shape rasterizer

`raster_shape_render` allocates a caller-owned transparent RGBA tile and fills
the flattened edges from `svg_shape_document`. Geometry remains in user space;
the root viewBox maps it to the tile with the parsed `preserveAspectRatio`
alignment and `meet`, `slice`, or `none` behavior. The default is centered
`xMidYMid meet`. Nested `<svg>` viewport clips are carried by the shape
document. Each pixel uses a deterministic 4x4 grid at offsets
`{0.125, 0.375, 0.625, 0.875}` on each axis. For each shape, a sample is
covered only when it is inside the shape and inside every clip in its chain.
Pixel coverage is the rounded fraction of those 16 covered samples. A gradient
is evaluated once at the pixel center, and that color is used for every
covered sample; translucent gradient samples keep source-over compositing.
Final RGB is averaged over nontransparent sample colors and alpha is averaged
across all 16 samples. Fully covered opaque pixels retain the exact paint color
and empty pixels stay transparent black. Edges are grouped by source element,
fill rules are evaluated per element, and later painted elements replace
earlier opaque fills at each subpixel before coverage is resolved. A
`fill="none"` element is parsed but does not erase earlier pixels. The output
tile must be empty when passed in.

`raster_shape_render_at` evaluates the document's bounded SMIL overlay at a
caller-supplied time. It clones the mutable geometry/color/stroke/transform
arrays needed for that frame, leaves source and decoded arrays unchanged, and
reuses the regular deterministic scalar renderer. Each rendered element has a
bounded transform-frame chain, including the authored transform, `<use>` or
symbol placement, and nested viewport mapping. Animated transforms replace the
authored transform by default, `additive="sum"` post-composes, and multiple
transform tracks compose in document order. Motion and numeric geometry are
applied in the target's user space before the same ancestor chain. Object-box
gradient bounds and per-instance clip transforms/bounds are refreshed on the
overlay; shared decoded clips are copied within a 64 MiB frame cap. Animated
path morphing returns `unsupported` because the scene stores flattened path
edges. Geometry or transform animation inside a filtered or masked opacity
group also returns `unsupported`; those effects need their own animated
coordinate update.

Embedded PNG/JPEG image fills sample provider-owned premultiplied RGBA8 with
bilinear interpolation in inverse-transformed local coordinates. Sampling is
bounded by the image viewport, source pixel dimensions, and clip chain; image
opacity is applied through the same isolated opacity groups as vector content.
Text reaches this renderer as flattened CoreText outline edges, so fill/stroke,
clips, transforms, and opacity follow the regular shape path.

After each element's fill, bounded strokes are tested against the same 4x4
sample grid. The stroke decoder stores each element's ordered edge range,
literal RGBA color, local width, inverse element transform, cap/join policy,
and bounded dash state.
Before rasterization, stroke intervals and joins are materialized once. A
conservative local-space grid narrows each sample to nearby stroke pieces;
segments include cap reach and joins include the miter-limit reach. Grid cells
are at least 1 user unit wide, each axis is at most 128 cells, and all shapes
share caps of 65,536 cells, 1,000,000 references, and 16 MiB of cache storage.
The dash builder is capped at 65,536 pieces per array and 1,000,000 build steps.
If a shape cannot be indexed within those bounds, it uses the bounded linear
stroke scan and the work preflight accounts for every piece tested. The
preflight also charges grid lookups and candidate pieces per sample, so sparse
paths no longer pay for every edge inside the path's full bounding rectangle.
The renderer computes a conservative device-space box for each shape's fill and
stroke. Stroke boxes include the transformed half-width, miter-limit reach,
square-cap reach, and a small floating-point margin. The box maps to every tile
pixel that can contain one of the 4x4 sample points. Empty and zero-area
geometry stays harmless; invalid or non-finite bounds conservatively select
the full tile. The one-bit boundary map marks pixels near every painted-shape
edge, with stroke reach included, and every clip child edge in each clipped
shape's full parent chain. Clip geometry is mapped through its element
transform into device space; object-bounding-box clip edges are first mapped
through the painted shape bounds. Edge boxes expand beyond the 4x4 sample
footprint to stay conservative. The center-sample fast path is used only
outside this map and outside partial viewport pixels, where no shape or clip
edge can cross the pixel. Gradient interior variation does not require marking
because gradient color is sampled at the pixel center.

Shapes are visited in source paint order and only over their clipped boxes.
A y-interval event set yields the shapes whose bounds intersect the current
row, avoiding a full shape-list scan for every tile row. A scanline event table
maintains each shape's fill edges whose half-open y-range contains each sample
row. The active set is emitted in original edge order;
the crossing arithmetic, winding/parity updates, color replacement, stroke
tests, sample locations, and final RGBA rounding keep the reference operation
order. The test-only `raster_shape_render_reference` has no boundary map or
center shortcut: it tests all 16 sample positions for every pixel against
every shape and clip, while evaluating gradient paint at the pixel center. It
serves as the byte-comparison oracle for production culling and scanline paths.

The renderer rejects invalid viewport data, malformed edge/group arrays, and
actual post-culling work above the existing 200,000,000-operation cap. The
checked work estimate includes tile pixels, summed shape-box pixels, painted
and clip edge boundary-map visits and pixel marks, scanline events and
active-edge visits, fill crossings, gradient-stop and clip-test work, and
stroke edge/dash work for each relevant sample. Checked arithmetic rejects overflow
and excessive work before rendering; quality is never reduced to satisfy the
cap. Temporary storage is bounded by shape/edge counts, tile dimensions, and
the output tile: the boundary map is one bit per tile pixel, sample buffers are
one row wide, and scanline events are at most two per edge. Rendering remains
single-threaded and deterministic. Output ownership
passes to the caller only on success, who releases it with `raster_tile_destroy`.

Element/group `opacity` is composited in isolated RGBA layers after the group
contents have painted. Nested layers composite source-over in document order.
Scratch tile bytes are checked and capped at 64 MiB; a request above the cap
returns a limit diagnostic instead of painting a partial frame.

## Raster modules

- `shape_render.c` validates the document, builds bounds and scanline state,
  enforces the existing checked work cap, and coordinates deterministic sample
  traversal and RGBA output.
- `shape_render_sample.c` evaluates one fill sample, applies clip membership and
  paint-server sampling, then composites the fill and stroke with the existing
  integer source-over operation. It preserves the test-only scalar alpha mode.
- `shape_render_stroke.c` materializes local stroke segments and tests caps,
  joins, miter limits, dash intervals, and closed-path dash seams.
- `shape_render_stroke_grid.c` builds and queries the bounded local-space stroke
  grid; the scalar reference remains an unindexed comparison path.
- `shape_render_group.c` renders isolated opacity subtrees using bounded tile
  scratch and composites each layer with source-over alpha.
- `shape_bounds.c` owns conservative device-space shape boxes and the boundary
  mask; `shape_scanline.c` owns row events and active-edge ordering.
- `shape_render_internal.h` carries private measurement and helper contracts;
  the public `shape_render.h` API is unchanged.

## Tile cache

`raster_tile_cache` is mutable from one owner thread and has no platform or shape-decoding dependencies. Its explicit byte cap is nonzero and at most 256 MiB. Accounted bytes include the complete preallocated entry array and every occupied tile's RGBA payload; creation rejects a slot array larger than the cap. LRU ties use stable slot order; a two-part monotonic tick preserves recency across tick rollover. Cache keys are caller supplied. Changing generation or integer scale bucket through `raster_tile_cache_set_epoch` clears all entries. A successful put transfers the tile's malloc-owned RGBA allocation and clears the caller's tile; a failed put leaves the caller's tile owned and unchanged. Lookup returns a borrowed tile valid until the next cache call that mutates LRU/cache state or destruction.

Filter primitives run in bounded RGBA surfaces inside isolated group layers.
Gaussian blur uses separable finite kernels; offsets, flood, blend, composite,
merge, color matrix, and drop shadow keep deterministic scalar channel
rounding. `linearRGB` input is converted from sRGB before primitives and
converted back afterward; `sRGB` bypasses that conversion. Filter evaluation
is capped at 50 million pixel-primitive work units and 64 MiB of scratch, in
addition to the enclosing group layer's 64 MiB budget. W5 effect fixtures
compare selected output with `rsvg-convert`.
# Source-backed SVG index

The index session borrows an immutable complete byte slice until destruction.
`svg_index_step` examines no more than the requested budget, capped at 64 KiB.
Element and name ranges refer directly to that slice; no source text is copied.
Mutable session state belongs to one owner thread. Cancellation and generation
changes are also owner-thread operations. A canceled session cannot be resumed.

The large-input path has independent limits (1 GiB source, depth 256, one
million elements and attributes, and 256 MiB combined element-record and
token-vector capacity (each vector is capped at half that budget). Index
records are owner-thread-only. A bounded task validates the complete source
with the same XML grammar and exposes its token spans after completion; worker
allocations are capped before retrying token output. The existing one-shot
tokenizer remains capped at 16 MiB and its defaults do not change.

Once a supported depth-one shape has a complete source range and the background
token stream has validated all bytes through that range, `first_preview_ready`
becomes true. The owner pauses element scanning while that prefix validation
catches up. An error before or inside the candidate span blocks publication; a
later malformed tail still allows the already validated preview while the
session reports failure. `svg_index_make_preview_source` returns an owned
minimal SVG consisting of the original root opener and shape span. Callers
schedule decode/raster work and must retain that owned byte buffer through task
completion.

The early preview subset requires an SVG root with supported `width` and
`height` attributes and an unprefixed `rect` or `path` whose attribute names
are accepted by the current shape decoder. Unsupported attributes such as
`transform`, element prefixes, and unsupported root attributes keep the source
record but mark it unsupported, allowing a later eligible shape to be chosen.
Start tags longer than 64 KiB remain indexed with their original spans but are
not scanned for early-preview eligibility; this keeps owner-thread attribute
inspection within the step budget. The UI marks a preview visible only after
the worker has produced its owned raster tile.
# SVG SMIL animation model

`smil.c` reads bounded animation values and simple timing controls;
`smil_tracks.c` associates supported animation elements with their target spans;
`motion_path.c` resolves local `<mpath>` references and flattens the line-only
motion-path subset; `evaluate.c` samples timing and interpolation without
changing source bytes. `svg_shape_document.animation` owns the track/keyframe
arrays and borrows every value and source span from `document.source`.

The model accepts up to 128 tracks, 256 key values per track, 128 stable
diagnostics, and a one-hour document timeline. It supports numeric geometry and
opacity properties, literal solid `fill`/`stroke` colors, `<set>`, the
`translate`/`scale`/`rotate`/`skewX`/`skewY` transform types, simple offset and
syncbase begin/end timing, repeat count/duration, `remove`/`freeze`, key times,
linear/spline/discrete/paced interpolation, and additive/accumulate for numeric
and color values. Motion paths accept local `path` or `mpath` references made
from one `M` plus `L`, `H`, `V`, and `Z` segments, with numeric, `auto`, and
`auto-reverse` rotation.

Event timing, CSS animation/transition rules, external motion references,
curved/arc motion paths, and malformed or over-limit tracks produce stable
diagnostic kinds and byte offsets. `<animate attributeName="d">` is parsed only
when each key has the same path command/number structure; the current raster
overlay reports it unsupported because changing flattened curve topology is
not yet implemented. The renderer applies numeric and color overlays to leaf
shapes and composes transform/motion overlays through a bounded per-render-
instance ancestry chain. This includes groups, `<use>`/symbol placement, and
nested viewport mappings; animated transform replacement and additive sum are
kept distinct, and multiple transform tracks compose in document order.
Object-box gradients and clips update with animated bounds. Filtered/masked
opacity groups, active path morphing, geometry changes under patterns, and
group opacity animation still return stable unsupported results when their
flattened scene data cannot represent the update.

## Source authoring

authoring.c builds byte patches for supported SMIL values, key timing, and
easing. The patch owns its replacement buffer; its source is borrowed from the
decoded animation document until the patch has been built. Callers apply the
single patch with document_edit_replace_source_span, then destroy it.

Only bounded numeric, supported color, and transform animate /
animateTransform tracks with finite simple timing and no additive,
accumulated, sync-base, paced, path, or motion semantics are editable. A
property-value edit rewrites only the animation start tag, preserving all
unrelated tag bytes and every byte outside that tag. Key sequences are capped
at 256 values, tags and individual values at 64 KiB, and one patch at 1 MiB.
Rejected and no-op operations produce no patch. Easing handles are finite and
in [0,1]; an interval edit preserves the raw text of other spline tuples.

Spline tracks accept key edits and keep exactly key_count-1 keySplines tuples,
passing each tuple's raw bytes through unchanged. A value edit or key move
keeps all tuples. Adding a key splits an interval and repeats that interval's
tuple. Deleting key 0 drops tuple 0, the last key drops the last tuple, and any
other key k drops tuple k. Deleting a spline track down to one key removes
keySplines and sets calcMode="linear", because a one-key spline track does not
parse. A keySplines or values result over 64 KiB returns the limit error before
any patch exists. Tuples are copied raw, so whitespace padding the parser
trims can make the output exceed 64 KiB (an add_key that duplicates a padded
tuple); the edge test covers this limit path. authoring_create.c holds track creation; both files share
authoring_internal.h.

Track creation returns one bounded animate fragment with explicit initial
and authored values, begin="0s", finite duration, and linear interpolation.
The editor inserts/removes it with the document edit transaction API. The
caller supplies the selected property's current typed value as the time-zero
seed; static field edits never call this module implicitly.

# Corpus provenance and exclusions

## Included fixtures

The initial 24 fixtures are authored for Vexel in this work order. Their
`source_origin` and `source_revision` are `project-authored`, their source hash
is the exact local file hash, and their license is MPL-2.0. They are synthetic
coverage examples, not representative user documents. No external source file
was adapted. Creation timestamp, feature tags, path, content hash, license URL
and license hash are recorded per fixture in `bench/corpus/manifest.json`.

The project license text is `bench/corpus/licenses/MPL-2.0.txt`; its SHA-256 is
`3f3d9e0024b1921b067d6f7f88deb4a60cbe7a78e76c64e3f1d7fc3b779b9d04`.

## Pinned WPT license review

The reviewed upstream is Web Platform Tests revision
`da1355b3fc629f97f8194884ab113da1ba3c7990`. Its root license notice was
retrieved from
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/da1355b3fc629f97f8194884ab113da1ba3c7990/LICENSE.md`
on 2026-10-08 and is retained verbatim as
`bench/corpus/licenses/WPT-LICENSE.md`. The file is 1,500 bytes and its
SHA-256 is
`5fac07febb0e2a97fb0d7b0def149ec08b642e1ba4b9c345283ab1cbd2af6570`.
This is the 3-Clause BSD notice for WPT at that exact revision. It remains
separate from the MPL-2.0 project fixtures. No WPT test file is included in
this first corpus, so no upstream test source hash or modification status is
claimed for a fixture.

## Exclusions

- The archived W3C SVG 1.1 test suite is excluded. Its rights page points to a
  W3C Document License and W3C Member Agreement; this work order establishes no
  per-file reuse grant. Rights statement:
  https://www.w3.org/Graphics/SVG/Test/Overview.html
- W3C test-suite material generally is excluded absent a specific applicable
  grant. Policy: https://www.w3.org/copyright/test-suites-licenses/
- WPT `svg/import/` is excluded, along with any file with unclear/conflicting
  per-file rights, external linked resources, executable script behavior,
  proprietary/user provenance, or GPL SVG-editor origin. None was copied.
- Natural/customer SVGs and large generated stress families are excluded.
  The small authored stress fixtures only exercise deterministic feature
  coverage and are not a benchmark-size tier.

The corpus is intended for development checks only. It does not establish W3C
conformance and no public performance claim should be made from this subset.
# Local SVG references

The reference module borrows immutable source bytes and decoder tokens. It
builds a fixed-capacity open-addressed ID index with 131,072 `uint32_t` slots
(512 KiB), independent of source length and ID count, and rejects more than
65,536 IDs or duplicate IDs. It recognizes only `href="#id"` and correctly
root-bound `xlink:href="#id"`; missing IDs, external URLs, malformed
references, cycles, and unsupported targets return stable `unsupported`
diagnostics. It never loads external resources.

The index maps IDs to token offsets in the original source. `traverse.c`
resolves live uses by recursively walking those tokens at the use position. No
subtree copy, rewritten source buffer, generated wrapper, second tokenizer
array, or diagnostic source map is used. Diagnostics therefore retain their
original source byte offsets. Reference traversal bounds and inheritance are
documented in `../shape/traverse-README.md`.

`<defs>` and uninstantiated `<symbol>` subtrees do not paint. Referenced groups,
basic shapes, and symbols support use-site translation, symbol viewBox mapping,
inherited paint, and nested references subject to depth, instance, and work
caps. A referenced source span is limited to 64 KiB, with a 1 MiB aggregate
span-visit budget per decode. These counters bound repeated traversal; they do
not trigger any source copy. The original source remains borrowed and unchanged. SVG 2 Document
Structure was consulted 2026-10-09. The implementation is original project
code.

Attribute validation includes stroke-capable paths and basic shapes, rounded
rectangle `rx`/`ry`, CSS presentation values, and nested `<svg>` viewport
attributes. Text validation includes `xml:space` and the supported font, text
anchor, and spacing properties; image hrefs are accepted only by the media-aware
shape decoder when they use the supported embedded Base64 PNG/JPEG form.
Unsupported attributes still fail with the original token's source offset.
Nested viewBox mappings and viewport clipping are performed by shape traversal;
this module only indexes and validates local references.

Root `xmlns:*` declarations and unknown prefixed export metadata (for example
Inkscape labels or Illustrator layer tags) are ignored for rendering while the
borrowed source remains unchanged. A prefixed spelling of a recognized SVG
paint or geometry attribute remains unsupported, so foreign metadata cannot
silently override SVG semantics. `xlink:href` continues to be accepted only
for validated local references.

W5 local filter, mask, pattern, and marker references resolve through the same
source-backed ID table. Their definition spans stay in the original token
array; the resolver does not rewrite source bytes or fetch external resources.
# SVG clip paths

The clip module resolves a local `clip-path: url(#id)` to a bounded set of
basic shapes or paths, decodes those shapes into an owned scalar geometry
document, and tests point membership as a union. The rasterizer intersects that
union with each covered fill sample. The decoded clip and its temporary source
are owned by the parent shape document and released with it.

Before copying clip-child source, the resolver computes each definition and
child style through the document CSS cascade. Nested `clip-path` declarations
and other matched paint properties are rejected with a stable `unsupported`
diagnostic, including declarations supplied by class selectors.

`clipPathUnits` supports `userSpaceOnUse` (the SVG default) and
`objectBoundingBox`. User-space clips are sampled in the declaring element's
user space, including ancestor and `<use>` transforms. Object bounding boxes
come from the declaring element's untransformed local geometry and are then
mapped through its transform. A group or `<use>` clip uses the AABB of its
whole rendered subtree and is resolved once for that declaration. Child clips
intersect with enclosing group/use clips; `clip-path` does not pass down as an
inherited style property.

Each clip is limited to 64 direct children, 65,536 flattened edges per clip,
64 KiB per referenced child span, and 512 KiB of clip-child scratch copies per
decode job. The wrapper prefix is formatted into a 192-byte stack buffer; its
actual bytes, the six-byte `</svg>` suffix, the referenced span, and the NUL
terminator count toward the scratch budget. The copied child span is never
modified in the original document. Oversized references return a stable
`limit` diagnostic. Nested `clip-path` declarations inside clip geometry,
empty clips, unsupported child syntax, singular transforms, and external
references fail with stable diagnostics. The raster work budget includes clip
edge tests.

The module also exposes an owned four-corner rectangle clip used by nested SVG
viewports. Shape traversal maps that rectangle through the active viewport
transform and attaches it to every descendant shape in the viewport range;
this clip intersects with the shape's other clips during raster sampling.

Each resolved clip records its rendered transform-frame owner rather than only
the source byte offset. This distinguishes separate `<use>` instances of the
same source element. Animation overlays deep-copy shared clip chains within a
64 MiB per-frame cap, update the owning inverse transform, and refresh
object-box bounds after local geometry changes. Nested viewport rectangles use
the owning frame before its viewBox suffix so their clip stays in the viewport
coordinate system.

The 512 KiB budget allows about 1,700 standalone shape clips when each
generated copy is about 300 bytes. Group clips consume one copy per declaring
group regardless of its child shape count. Scratch is still charged once per
clip declaration, including declarations inside separate `<use>` instances.

No external resources or renderer source are loaded or copied. Clip-child
scratch allocation obeys ADR-0014; the original document is never modified.
`clipPathUnits` defaults and clip geometry follow the W3C
[CSS Masking Module Level 1](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-masking-1/) section 6.1
(consulted 2026-10-09); the prior SVG 2 masking chapter now points to this
specification.
